subject: Physics
front: Physics vs Chemistry First Law Sign Convention Trap!
back: In Physics: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW (W > 0 when gas EXPANDS). In Chemistry: ΔU = q + w (w > 0 when work is done ON the gas, i.e., compression).

subject: Chemistry
front: Why does H₂O have a higher boiling point than HF despite F being more electronegative than O?
back: Each H₂O molecule forms up to 4 H-bonds (2 donors + 2 lone pairs) forming a 3D network, whereas HF forms only 2 H-bonds per molecule in zig-zag chains.

subject: Biology
front: Which strand of DNA is used as the template for mRNA transcription, and in which direction is mRNA synthesized?
back: DNA-dependent RNA polymerase always polymerizes mRNA in 5' → 3' direction using the 3' → 5' template strand. The coding strand (5' → 3') has the same sequence as mRNA (with T instead of U).

subject: Physics
front: Mirror formula vs Lens formula sign trap for focal length & magnification!
back: Mirror: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, m = -v/u. Lens: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f, m = +v/u. Always apply Cartesian sign convention to known quantities ONLY, never to the unknown!

subject: Chemistry
front: Why is Cr²⁺ a strong reducing agent while Mn³⁺ is a strong oxidizing agent (both d⁴)?
back: Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ achieves stable half-filled t₂g³ configuration in aqueous solution. Mn³⁺ → Mn²⁺ achieves stable half-filled d⁵ configuration.

subject: Biology
front: In C₄ plants, where are PEPcase and RuBisCO located respectively?
back: PEPcase is in Mesophyll cells (RuBisCO is ABSENT here). RuBisCO is exclusively in Bundle Sheath cells (PEPcase is absent here).
